newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says pregnancy not a guarantee against dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Court says pregnancy not a guarantee against dismissal.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday women suffering a pregnancy-related illness are not guaranteed protection from dismissal under the European Union law granting equal access to employment.
A Danish supermarket worker, on sick leave twice during her pregnancy and who required an extended leave to recover from a pregnancy-related illness, was dismissed by her employer.
Helle Larsson was gone from her workplace for a total of 14 months, including sick leave, maternity leave, annual leave and again on sick leave.

"Outside the periods of maternity leave laid down by member states...a woman is not protected under the directive against dismissal on grounds of periods of absence due to an illness originating in pregnancy," the court said.

"As...male and female workers are equally exposed to illness, the directive does not concern illnesses attributable to pregnancy or confinement. The principle of equal treatment enshrined in the directive does not, therefore, preclude account being taken of a woman's absence from work" while she is pregnant, but before maternity leave begins, when calculating grounds for dismissal.
Reference from the So-og Handelsret, Denmark for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings between
Handels- og Kontofunktionaerernes Forbund i Danmark, acting on behalf of Helle Elisabeth Larsson
Dansk Handel & Service, acting on behalf of Fotex Supermarked A/S

on the interpretation of articles 5(1) and 2(1) of Council directive 76/207 on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment for men and women as regards access to employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions

Without prejudice to the provisions of national law adopted pursuant to article 2(3) of Council directive 76/207 on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment for men and women as regards access to employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions, article 5(1), in conjunction with article 2(1), of that directive does not preclude dismissals which are the result of absences due to an illness attributable to pregnancy or confinement, even where that illness arose during pregnancy and continued during and after maternity leave.
